title: What drug and alcohol training do transit agencies need under 49 CFR 655.14?
description: 49 CFR 655.14 explained: 60 minutes of drug training for every covered transit employee, 60 plus 60 minutes for supervisors, policy rules and record keeping.
shortAnswer: Under 49 CFR 655.14, every employer covered by the Federal Transit Administration drug and alcohol rule must give each covered employee at least 60 minutes of training on the effects and consequences of prohibited drug use and its signs and symptoms, display and distribute informational material and a hotline number, and train supervisors who make reasonable suspicion decisions for at least 60 minutes on drug indicators and 60 minutes on alcohol indicators. Training records are kept for two years.
keyTakeaways: 49 CFR Part 655 applies to recipients and subrecipients of FTA funding under 49 U.S.C. 5307, 5309 or 5311 and their contractors that perform safety sensitive functions (49 CFR 655.3).

Every covered employee needs at least 60 minutes of drug training on effects, consequences, and signs and symptoms; Part 655 does not set an equivalent alcohol training minimum for employees (49 CFR 655.14(b)(1)).
Supervisors and officials authorized to make reasonable suspicion determinations need at least 60 minutes on drug use indicators and 60 minutes on alcohol misuse indicators (49 CFR 655.14(b)(2)).
The policy statement must be adopted by the local governing board, cover ten listed elements and be given in writing to every covered employee and employee organization (49 CFR 655.15 and 655.16).
Training records, including names, dates and times of attendance and a certification that training complies, are kept for two years (49 CFR 655.71).
regulator: Federal Transit Administration (FTA), U.S. Department of Transportation, under 49 CFR Part 655 and the testing procedures in 49 CFR Part 40
appliesTo: Recipients and subrecipients of FTA funds under 49 U.S.C. 5307, 5309 or 5311, including urban and rural transit agencies
Contractors that provide a safety sensitive service for a recipient, subrecipient, employer or operator
Covered employees, including applicants, transferees and certain volunteers
Supervisors and company officials authorized to make reasonable suspicion determinations

sections.heading: Which transit employers and employees does Part 655 cover?

blocks.text: Part 655 applies to every recipient and subrecipient of Federal assistance under 49 U.S.C. 5307, 5309 or 5311, and to any of their contractors, under [49 CFR 655.3](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/49/655.3). Two carve outs apply: commuter railroad operations regulated by the Federal Railroad Administration follow 49 CFR Part 219, and ferry operations that comply with U.S. Coast Guard testing rules are treated as in concurrent compliance with Part 655 testing requirements.
Coverage turns on function, not job title. Under [49 CFR 655.4](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/49/655.4), safety sensitive functions are:

items: Operating a revenue service vehicle, including when not in revenue service.
Operating a nonrevenue service vehicle when a commercial driver's license is required.
Controlling dispatch or movement of a revenue service vehicle.

Maintaining, including repairing, overhauling and rebuilding, a revenue service vehicle or equipment used in revenue service, with exceptions for certain smaller recipients that contract out maintenance.
Carrying a firearm for security purposes.

blocks.text: A covered employee includes applicants and transferees. A volunteer is covered if they must hold a commercial driver's license to operate the vehicle, or if they perform a safety sensitive function and receive remuneration beyond their actual expenses. Dispatchers, mechanics and armed security staff are therefore in scope for the 60 minute training alongside operators.

sections.heading: What does the 60 minute employee training requirement cover?

blocks.text: Every covered employee must receive at least 60 minutes of training on drug use, covering two subject areas. [49 CFR 655.14(b)(1)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-655.14) requires training on "the effects and consequences of prohibited drug use on personal health, safety, and the work environment, and on the signs and symptoms that may indicate prohibited drug use."
Three points often trip up transit training programs:

items: **It is drug training only.** Section 655.14 sets no minimum alcohol training duration for covered employees. Alcohol information reaches employees through the policy statement and the education component.
**It is a minimum duration, not a content limit.** Sixty minutes is the floor; content beyond that, such as the employer's own procedures, can be added.

**It is not stated as recurring.** Section 655.14 does not set a refresher interval, so any repeat cycle is the employer's decision and should be documented, for example using [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

blocks.text: Separately, the education component in 655.14(a) requires display and distribution to every covered employee of informational material and a community service hotline telephone number for employee assistance, if available.

sections.heading: What training do transit supervisors need?

blocks.text: Supervisors and other company officers authorized to make reasonable suspicion determinations need at least 60 minutes on drug use indicators and at least 60 minutes on alcohol misuse indicators. The two modules differ slightly in content under 655.14(b)(2).

blocks.caption: Supervisor training content under 49 CFR 655.14(b)(2)
head: Module
Minimum duration
Required indicators
rows: Physical, behavioral, speech and performance indicators

blocks.text: The testing rule makes the training a precondition. Under [49 CFR 655.43](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/49/655.43), a reasonable suspicion determination must be "based on specific, contemporaneous, articulable observations concerning the appearance, behavior, speech, or body odors of the covered employee", and the observations must be made by a supervisor or company official "who is trained in detecting the signs and symptoms of drug use and alcohol misuse."

Supervisors also need to know the timing rules in 655.43. Alcohol testing is only authorized just before, during or just after safety sensitive duty. If an alcohol test is not given within two hours of the determination, the employer must record why; after eight hours, attempts stop and the reasons are recorded. A good supervisor module includes writing an observation record against a scenario.

sections.heading: How does the policy statement connect to training?

blocks.text: The policy statement is the document employees are trained on, so its content defines much of what training must explain. Under 49 CFR 655.15 the local governing board must adopt the statement and make it available to each covered employee.

Section 655.15 lists the required elements: the person who answers employee questions; the employee categories covered; prohibited conduct; the circumstances for testing; testing procedures and safeguards; the requirement to submit to testing; what counts as a refusal; the consequences of a verified positive result or a 0.04 alcohol result, including immediate removal and evaluation by a substance abuse professional; the consequences of a 0.02 to under 0.04 result; and notice of any elements the employer adds beyond Part 655. Section 655.16 then requires written notice of the policies and procedures to every covered employee and to employee organization representatives.

blocks.title: Keep the layers separate
blocks.text: Training content that blends FTA requirements with the agency's own stricter rules without labeling them breaches 655.15(j), which requires the employer to inform employees of program elements not required by Part 655. Mark each employer authority rule clearly in both the policy and the training.

blocks.text: Under [49 CFR 655.71](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/49/655.71), records related to employee training are kept for two years from creation, in a secure location with controlled access. They must include the drug and alcohol training materials and a copy of the policy, the names of employees attending and the dates and times of training, documentation of supervisor reasonable suspicion training, and the compliance certification. See [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures the 655.14 subjects, the 655.15 policy elements and the 655.43 observation and timing rules as separate knowledge points linked to each safety sensitive function. A transit agency can then show auditors which content each operator, mechanic, dispatcher or supervisor received and when, with the attendance times 655.71 requires.

faqs.q: Does the FTA require annual refresher drug and alcohol training?
faqs.a: No. As at November 2026, 49 CFR 655.14 sets minimum durations for employee and supervisor training but does not state a refresher interval. Many agencies refresh training on a schedule of their choosing, which should be documented in their own policy and clearly identified as an employer requirement.

faqs.q: Must contractors' employees receive the 60 minute training?
faqs.a: Yes, when they perform safety sensitive functions. Under 49 CFR 655.4 an employer includes subrecipients, operators and contractors, and a covered employee is anyone who performs or will perform a safety sensitive function for an entity subject to Part 655. The recipient remains responsible for ensuring compliance.

faqs.q: Can supervisor training be combined into one two hour session?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the records show at least 60 minutes on drug indicators and at least 60 minutes on alcohol indicators, covering the speech indicators that apply only to the alcohol module. Section 655.71 requires documentation of supervisor training, so a timed agenda is the simplest proof.

faqs.q: How long must FTA training records be kept?
faqs.a: Two years from the date the record was created, under 49 CFR 655.71(b)(2). Verified positive results, refusals and substance abuse professional referrals are kept for five years, and negative results for one year.

factCheck.claim: Covered employees receive at least 60 minutes of training on effects and consequences of prohibited drug use and signs and symptoms; supervisors at least 60 minutes on physical, behavioral and performance indicators of drug use and 60 minutes on physical, behavioral, speech and performance indicators of alcohol misuse; education includes informational material and hotline number

Part 655 applies to recipients and subrecipients under 49 U.S.C. 5307, 5309 or 5311 and their contractors; FRA regulated railroad operations follow Part 219; USCG compliant ferries in concurrent compliance

Five safety sensitive functions (revenue vehicle operation, CDL nonrevenue vehicle operation, dispatch, maintenance, armed security); covered employee includes applicants, transferees and certain volunteers
Policy statement adopted by local governing board with listed elements (a) to (j), including notice of non-required elements
Written notice of policies to every covered employee and employee organization representatives
Reasonable suspicion based on specific, contemporaneous, articulable observations by a trained supervisor; alcohol testing only around duty; two hour record and eight hour cutoff

Training records kept two years; include training materials and policy, attendee names with dates and times, supervisor training documentation and compliance certification; positives and refusals five years; negatives one year
